summary: Before a war, the Kohen chosen for war speaks to the soldiers in Hebrew. He tells them not to be afraid of the enemy, because Hashem goes with them and fights for them.

chunks.en: The Kohen anointed for war,
chunks.st: the priest who was anointed for war,

words.note: The Kohen chosen to speak to the army.

chunks.en: when he speaks to the people,
chunks.st: at the time that he would speak to the nation,

chunks.en: would speak in Hebrew,
chunks.st: he would speak to them in the sacred tongue, Hebrew,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Devarim 20):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "And when you come close to the battle,
chunks.st: “And it shall be, when you draw near to the battle,

chunks.en: the Kohen shall come forward."
chunks.st: that the priest shall approach and speak to the people” (Deuteronomy 20:2).

chunks.en: This is the Kohen anointed for war.
chunks.st: This priest identified in the verse is the priest anointed for war,
chunks.stMore: the priest who is inaugurated specifically to serve this function.

chunks.en: "And he shall speak to the people" —
chunks.st: “And speak to the people”;

chunks.en: in Hebrew.
chunks.st: he addresses them in the sacred tongue, Hebrew.

chunks.en: "And he shall say to them (Devarim 20):
chunks.st: The Torah dictates the priest’s address: “And he shall say to them:

chunks.he: שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל אַתֶּם קְרֵבִים הַיּוֹם לַמִּלְחָמָה
chunks.en: Hear, Yisrael, you are coming close today to battle
chunks.st: Hear Israel,
chunks.stMore: you draw near today to battle against your enemies; let not your heart faint; fear not, nor be alarmed, and do not be terrified of them” (Deuteronomy 20:3).

chunks.en: against your enemies" —
chunks.st: The priest expounds: “Against your enemies”

chunks.en: and not against your brothers.
chunks.st: and not against your brothers.

chunks.en: It is not Yehudah against Shimon,
chunks.st: This is not a war of the tribe of Judah against Simon

chunks.en: and not Shimon against Binyamin,
chunks.st: and not Simon against Benjamin,

chunks.en: that if you fall into their hands, they will have mercy on you,
chunks.st: such that if you fall into their hands your brothers will have mercy on you,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Divrei Hayamim II 28):
chunks.st: as it is stated
chunks.stMore: with regard to a war between Judah and Israel:

chunks.en: "And the men who were named got up,
chunks.st: “And the men that have been mentioned by name rose up,

chunks.en: and they took the captives,
chunks.st: and took the captives,

chunks.en: and dressed from the spoils all who had no clothes;
chunks.st: and with the spoil clothed all that were naked among them,

chunks.en: they dressed them and gave them shoes,
chunks.st: and arrayed them, and shod them,

chunks.en: gave them food and drink, and anointed them,
chunks.st: and gave them to eat and to drink, and anointed them,

chunks.en: and led all the weak ones on donkeys,
chunks.st: and carried all the feeble of them upon donkeys,

chunks.en: and brought them to Yericho, the city of date palms,
chunks.st: and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees,

chunks.en: to their brothers, and they went back to Shomron."
chunks.st: unto their brethren; then they returned to Samaria” (II Chronicles 28:15).

chunks.en: But you are going against your enemies,
chunks.st: Rather, you are marching to war against your enemies,

chunks.he: שֶׁאִם תִּפְּלוּ בְיָדָם אֵין מְרַחֲמִין עֲלֵיכֶם.
chunks.en: and if you fall into their hands, they will not have mercy on you.
chunks.st: and if you fall into their hands, they will not have mercy on you.

chunks.en: "Do not let your heart be soft, do not fear,
chunks.st: The priest continues: “Let not your heart faint; fear not,

chunks.en: and do not panic..." (Devarim 20).
chunks.st: nor be alarmed,
chunks.stMore: and do not be terrified of them” (Deuteronomy 20:3).

chunks.en: "Do not let your heart be soft" —
chunks.st: “Let not your heart faint”

chunks.en: because of the horses neighing and the swords being sharpened.
chunks.st: due to the neighing of horses and the sharpening of the enemy’s swords.

chunks.en: "Do not fear" —
chunks.st: “Fear not”

chunks.en: because of the banging of shields and the noise of boots.
chunks.st: due to the knocking of shields [terisin] and the noise of their boots [calgassin].

chunks.en: "Do not panic" —
chunks.st: “Nor be alarmed”

chunks.en: because of the sound of the horns.
chunks.st: by the sound of trumpets.

chunks.en: "Do not be scared" —
chunks.st: “Do not be terrified”

chunks.en: because of the sound of shouting.
chunks.st: due to the sound of shouts.

chunks.en: "For Hashem your God is the One Who goes with you."
chunks.st: The priest explains why the soldiers need not be terrified. “For the Lord your God is He that goes with you,
chunks.stMore: to fight for you against your enemies, to save you” (Deuteronomy 20:4).

chunks.he: הֵן בָּאִין בְּנִצְחוֹנוֹ שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם,
chunks.en: They come relying on the strength of a person (flesh and blood),
chunks.st: Remember that they come to war championed by flesh and blood,

chunks.en: and you come relying on the strength of Hashem.
chunks.st: and you are coming championed by the Omnipresent.

words.note: Literally "the Place", a name for Hashem.

chunks.en: The Pelishtim came relying on Golyas.
chunks.st: The Philistines came championed by Goliath.

chunks.en: What happened to him in the end?
chunks.st: What was his end?

chunks.en: In the end he fell by the sword, and they fell with him.
chunks.st: In the end, he fell by the sword, and they fell with him (see I Samuel, chapter 17).

chunks.he: בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן בָּאוּ בְנִצְחוֹנוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹבַךְ,
chunks.en: Bnei Ammon came relying on Shovach.
chunks.st: The Ammonites came championed by Shobach.

chunks.en: What happened to him in the end?
chunks.st: What was his end?

chunks.en: In the end he fell by the sword, and they fell with him.
chunks.st: In the end, he fell by the sword, and they fell with him (see II Samuel, chapter 10).

chunks.en: But you are not like that.
chunks.st: But as for you, you are not so, reliant upon the strength of mortals:

chunks.en: "For Hashem your God is the One Who goes with you
chunks.st: “For the Lord your God is He that goes with you,

chunks.en: to fight for you..."
chunks.st: to fight for you against your enemies, to save you”;

chunks.en: This is the camp of the Aron.
chunks.explain: The Aron went out to war with them.
chunks.st: this verse is referring to the camp of the Ark
chunks.stMore: of the Covenant that accompanies them out to war.

summary: Before a war, the officers send some men home: one who built a new house, planted a vineyard, or got engaged, and did not yet get to enjoy it. They still help the army with water, food and roads.
stIntro: The mishna continues its discussion of the speech given before battle.

chunks.en: "And the officers shall speak to the people, saying:
chunks.st: “And the officers shall speak to the people, saying:

chunks.he: מִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה בַיִת חָדָשׁ
chunks.en: Who is the man who built a new house
chunks.st: What man is there that has built a new house,

chunks.en: and has not yet started living in it?
chunks.st: and has not dedicated it?

chunks.en: Let him go back home..."
chunks.st: Let him go and return to his house,
chunks.stMore: lest he die in the battle, and another man dedicate it” (Deuteronomy 20:5).

chunks.en: It is the same whether he built a barn for straw,
chunks.st: He is sent home if he is one who builds a storehouse for straw,

chunks.en: a barn for cattle,
chunks.st: a barn for cattle,

chunks.en: a shed for wood,
chunks.st: a shed for wood, or

chunks.en: or a storehouse.
chunks.st: a warehouse.

chunks.en: Whether he built it,
chunks.st: Similarly, it applies if he is one who builds,

chunks.en: or bought it,
chunks.st: or if he is one who purchases,

chunks.en: or inherited it,
chunks.st: or if he is one who inherits,

chunks.en: or it was given to him as a present.
chunks.st: or if he is one to whom it is given as a gift.
chunks.stMore: In all these instances, the man returns from the war encampment.

chunks.en: "And who is the man who planted a vineyard
chunks.st: The next verse states: “And what man is there that has planted a vineyard,

chunks.en: and has not yet used its fruit..."
chunks.st: and has not used the fruit
chunks.stMore: thereof? Let him go and return unto his house, lest he die in the battle and another man use the fruit thereof” (Deuteronomy 20:6).

chunks.en: Whether he planted a whole vineyard,
chunks.st: He is sent home if he is one who plants a whole vineyard of many vines,

chunks.en: or planted just five fruit trees,
chunks.st: or if he is one who plants as few as five fruit trees of another variety,

chunks.en: even from five different kinds.
chunks.st: and even if these five are from the five species. The produce need not be all of one species.

chunks.en: Whether he planted it,
chunks.st: The same applies if he is one who plants,

chunks.en: or bent a branch into the ground to grow a new vine,
chunks.st: or if he is one who layers
chunks.stMore: the vine, bending a branch into the ground so that it may take root and grow as a new vine,

chunks.en: or grafted a branch onto a tree,
chunks.st: or if he is one who grafts different trees onto one another.

chunks.en: or bought it,
chunks.st: And it applies if he is one who purchases a vineyard,

chunks.en: or inherited it,
chunks.st: or if he is one who inherits a vineyard,

chunks.en: or it was given to him as a present.
chunks.st: or if he is one to whom the vineyard is given as a gift.

chunks.he: וּמִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה וְגוֹ' (שם).
chunks.en: "And who is the man who got engaged to a wife..."
chunks.st: The next verse states: “And what man is there that has betrothed a wife,
chunks.stMore: and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man take her” (Deuteronomy 20:7).

chunks.en: Whether he got engaged to a girl who was never married,
chunks.st: He is sent home if he is one who betroths a virgin,

chunks.en: or to a widow,
chunks.st: or if he is one who betroths a widow.

chunks.en: even a widow waiting for him as her yavam,
chunks.st: This applies even if his yevama, his late brother’s wife, is a widow waiting for him as her yavam to perform levirate marriage;

words.note: Her husband's brother, who may marry her when her husband died with no children.

chunks.en: and even if he heard that his brother died in the war,
chunks.st: and even if he heard that his brother died in the war
chunks.stMore: and the widow begins to wait for him only then,

chunks.en: he goes back home.
chunks.st: he returns and goes home.

chunks.en: All these men hear the words of the Kohen
chunks.st: Each of these men, although they are exempt, still hear the address of the priest and

chunks.en: about the rules of war, and go home,
chunks.st: the regulations of war at the local camp, and thereafter they return to their respective homes.

chunks.he: וּמְסַפְּקִין מַיִם וּמָזוֹן וּמְתַקְּנִין אֶת הַדְּרָכִים:
chunks.en: and they bring water and food and fix the roads.
chunks.st: However, they still support the war effort, and they provide water and food for the soldiers and repair the roads.

summary: Some men are not sent home from the war: one who built only a small building, planted fewer than five fruit trees, married his divorced wife again, or got engaged to someone he is not allowed to marry.

chunks.en: And these men do not go home:
chunks.st: And these are the men who do not return to their homes:

chunks.en: one who builds a gatehouse,
chunks.st: One who builds a gateway, or

chunks.en: a porch, or a balcony;
chunks.st: an enclosed veranda [akhsadra], or a balcony; or

chunks.en: one who plants four fruit trees,
chunks.st: one who plants no more than four fruit trees

chunks.en: or five trees that do not give fruit;
chunks.st: or even five or more non-fruit bearing trees; or

chunks.en: one who marries his divorced wife again;
chunks.st: one who remarries his divorced
chunks.stMore: wife. Nor is there an exemption for one who has betrothed a woman whom he is not permitted to marry: With regard to

chunks.en: a widow (engaged) to a Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: a widow betrothed to a High Priest (see Leviticus 21:7);

chunks.en: a divorced woman or a chalutzah to a regular Kohen,
chunks.st: a divorcée or a yevama who performed ḥalitza [ḥalutza], in lieu of entering into a levirate marriage, betrothed to a common priest (see Leviticus 21:13–15);

chunks.en: a mamzeres or a nesinah to a Yisrael,
chunks.st: a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman betrothed to an Israelite;

words.note: A girl born from a forbidden relationship.
A girl from the Givonim, who may not marry into the Jewish people.

chunks.en: a Jewish girl to a mamzer or a nasin —
chunks.st: or an Israelite woman betrothed to a mamzer or a Gibeonite (see Deuteronomy 23:3);

chunks.en: he does not go home.
chunks.st: such a man does not return to his home.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Even one who builds a house again in its old place
chunks.st: Even one who rebuilds a house as it stood originally

chunks.en: does not go home.
chunks.st: would not return.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: Even one who builds a brick house in the Sharon
chunks.explain: Brick houses there often fell down.
chunks.st: Even one who builds a new brick house in the Sharon

chunks.en: does not go home.
chunks.st: would not return
chunks.stMore: because these houses are not stable and are expected to collapse periodically.

summary: Some men do not even go to the army camp: in the first year after building a house, using a new vineyard, or getting married.

chunks.en: These men do not even move from their place:
chunks.st: These are the men who do not even move from their places because they do not even report to the camp:

chunks.en: one who built a house and started living in it,
chunks.st: One who built a house and dedicated it within the year;

chunks.en: planted a vineyard and started using its fruit,
chunks.st: one who planted a vineyard and used its fruit for less than a year;

chunks.en: one who marries the woman he was engaged to,
chunks.st: one who marries his betrothed

chunks.en: one who marries his yevamah,
chunks.st: and one who marries his yevama,
chunks.stMore: his brother’s widow who must enter into a levirate marriage or perform ḥalitza,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Devarim 24):
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out with the army…

chunks.en: "He shall be free for his house for one year."
chunks.st: he shall be free for his house one year,
chunks.stMore: and shall cheer his wife whom he has taken” (Deuteronomy 24:5).

chunks.en: "For his house" — this means his house.
chunks.st: The mishna interprets the verse as follows: “For his house”; this means his house that he built.

chunks.en: "He shall be" — this means his vineyard.
chunks.st: “He shall be”; this term includes his vineyard.

chunks.en: "And he shall make his wife happy" —
chunks.st: “And shall cheer his wife”;

chunks.en: this means his wife.
chunks.st: this is his wife.

chunks.en: "Whom he has taken" —
chunks.st: “Whom he has taken”;

chunks.en: this includes his yevamah.
chunks.st: this phrase comes to include his yevama,
chunks.stMore: who is considered his wife with respect to this halakha although he has not yet married her.

chunks.en: They do not bring water and food,
chunks.st: Those who are exempt for these reasons do not even provide water and food to the soldiers,

chunks.en: and they do not fix the roads.
chunks.st: and they do not repair the roads.

summary: A man who is "afraid and soft-hearted" also goes home. Rabbi Akiva says this means someone scared of battle. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says it means someone afraid because of his sins, and the other reasons let him leave without being embarrassed.
stIntro: The mishna continues its discussion of the speech given before battle.

chunks.en: (Devarim 20) "And the officers shall speak more
chunks.st: “And the officers shall speak further

chunks.en: to the people,
chunks.st: to the people,

chunks.en: and say: Who is the man
chunks.st: and they shall say: What man is there

chunks.en: who is afraid and soft-hearted?
chunks.st: that is fearful and fainthearted?

chunks.en: Let him go back home."
chunks.st: Let him go and return unto his house” (Deuteronomy 20:8).

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: "Afraid and soft-hearted"
chunks.st: “That is fearful and fainthearted”

chunks.en: means just what it says: one who cannot
chunks.st: is to be understood as it indicates, that the man is unable

chunks.en: stand in the battle lines
chunks.st: to stand in the battle ranks

chunks.en: and see a sword pulled out.
chunks.st: and to see a drawn sword because it will terrify him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

chunks.en: "Afraid and soft-hearted" — this is
chunks.st: “That is fearful and fainthearted”; this is

chunks.en: one who is afraid because of the sins he has done.
chunks.st: one who is afraid because of the sins that he has; he, too, returns.

chunks.en: That is why the Torah gave him
chunks.st: Therefore, the Torah provided him with

chunks.en: all these (other reasons),
chunks.st: all these
chunks.stMore: additional reasons for exemption from the army

chunks.en: so he can say he is going home because of them.
chunks.explain: Then no one knows he is going home because of his sins.
chunks.st: so he can ascribe his leaving to one of them.
chunks.stMore: In this way, the sinner may leave the ranks without having to publicly acknowledge that he is a sinner.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.stMore: With regard to one who has betrothed a woman forbidden to him, including

chunks.en: A widow (engaged) to a Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: a widow betrothed to a High Priest;

chunks.en: a divorced woman or a chalutzah to a regular Kohen,
chunks.st: a divorcée or a yevama who performed ḥalitza [ḥalutza] betrothed to a common priest;

chunks.en: a mamzeres or a nesinah to a Yisrael,
chunks.st: a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman betrothed to an Israelite;

chunks.en: a Jewish girl to a mamzer or a nasin —
chunks.st: or a daughter of an Israelite betrothed to a mamzer or a Gibeonite;

chunks.en: he is the one who is "afraid and soft-hearted."
chunks.explain: He is afraid his sin will hurt him in the war.
chunks.st: this man is he whom the verse calls “fearful and fainthearted.”
chunks.stMore: He fears that his sin will jeopardize his safety in the war.

summary: After the speeches, officers stand in front of and behind the army to stop anyone from running away, because running away is how a battle is lost.
stIntro: The mishna continues its discussion. The verse states:

chunks.en: (Devarim 20) "And when the officers finish
chunks.st: “And it shall be, when the officers conclude

chunks.en: speaking to the people,
chunks.st: speaking to the people,

chunks.en: they shall appoint army captains at the head of the people,"
chunks.st: that captains of legions shall be appointed at the head of the people” (Deuteronomy 20:9).

chunks.en: and also at the back of the people.
chunks.st: The mishna adds: As well as at the rear of the people.

chunks.en: They put guards in front of them,
chunks.st: The officers station guards [zekifin] in front of them,

chunks.en: and others behind them,
chunks.st: and other guards behind them,

chunks.en: with iron sticks in their hands.
chunks.st: and they have iron rods [kashilin] in their hands.

chunks.en: And anyone who tries to turn back,
chunks.st: And with regard to anyone who attempts to turn back and flee from the war,

chunks.en: the guard may hit his legs,
chunks.st: the guard has license to beat [lekape’aḥ] his legs

chunks.en: because running away is the start of falling,
chunks.st: because the beginning of fleeing is a downfall on the battlefield,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Shmuel I 4):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Yisrael ran away from the Pelishtim,
chunks.st: “Israel has fled before the Philistines,

chunks.en: and there was also a great plague among the people."
chunks.st: and there has been also a great slaughter among the people” (I Samuel 4:17),

chunks.en: And later on it says (Shmuel I 31):
chunks.st: and likewise it says further on:

chunks.en: "And the men of Yisrael ran away from the Pelishtim
chunks.st: “And the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines,

chunks.en: and fell dead..."
chunks.st: and fell down slain in Mount Gilboa” (I Samuel 31:1).

summary: Sending these men home is only in a war of choice. In a war that is a mitzvah, everyone goes out, even a chassan and a kallah. Rabbi Yehuda uses different names for the two kinds of war.

chunks.en: When is all this said?
chunks.st: In what case are all of these statements, with regard to the various exemptions from war, said?

chunks.en: In a war of choice.
chunks.st: They are said with regard to elective wars.

chunks.en: But in a war that is a mitzvah,
chunks.st: But in wars whose mandate is a mitzva,

chunks.en: everyone goes out,
chunks.st: everyone goes,

chunks.en: even a chassan from his room and a kallah from her chuppah.
chunks.st: even a groom from his room and a bride from her wedding canopy.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: When is all this said?
chunks.st: In what case are all of these statements, with regard to the various exemptions from war, said?

chunks.en: In a war that is a mitzvah.
chunks.st: They are said with regard to wars whose mandate is a mitzva.

chunks.en: But in a war that must be fought,
chunks.st: But in obligatory wars,

chunks.en: everyone goes out,
chunks.st: everyone goes,

chunks.en: even a chassan from his room and a kallah from her chuppah.
chunks.st: even a groom from his room and a bride from her wedding canopy.
